arxiv-2007-04068.title: Decolonial AI: Decolonial Theory as Sociotechnical Foresight in Artificial Intelligence Journal: Philosophy and Technology
arxiv-2007-04068.creator: Shakir Mohamed*, Marie-Therese Png*, William Isaac*
arxiv-2007-04068.description: Abstract This paper explores the important role of critical science, and in particular of post-colonial and decolonial theories, in understanding and shaping the ongoing advances in artificial intelligence. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is viewed as amongst the technological advances that will reshape modern societies and their relations.

arxiv-2104-03113.title: Scaling Scaling Laws with Board Games
arxiv-2104-03113.creator: Andy L. Jones
arxiv-2104-03113.description: Abstract The largest experiments in machine learning now require resources far beyond the budget of all but a few institutions. Fortunately, it has recently been shown that the results of these huge experiments can often be extrapolated from the results of a sequence of far smaller, cheaper experiments.

arxiv-2203-05722.title: Self-interfering dynamics in Bose-Einstein condensates with engineered dispersions Journal: Physics Letters A
arxiv-2203-05722.creator: Jin Su 1,2 , Hao Lyu 3 , and Yongping Zhang 1
arxiv-2203-05722.description: Abstract Optical lattice and spin-orbit coupling are typical experimental approaches to engineer dispersion. We reveal a self-interfering dynamics in a noninteracting Bose-Einstein condensate with the engineered dispersion by optical lattice or spin-orbit coupling. The self-interference results from the co-occupation of positive and negative effect mass regimes in the engineered dispersion.

arxiv-2305-11526.title: Enhancing Short-Term Wind Speed Forecasting using Graph Attention and Frequency-Enhanced Mechanisms
arxiv-2305-11526.creator: Hao Liu, Huimin Ma, Tianyu Hu
arxiv-2305-11526.description: Abstract The safe and stable operation of power systems is greatly challenged by the high variability and randomness of wind power in large-scale wind-power-integrated grids. Wind power forecasting is an effective solution to tackle this issue, with wind speed forecasting being an essential aspect.

arxiv-2311-00776.title: Multi-mode Brownian Dynamics of a Nanomechanical Resonator in a Viscous Fluid
arxiv-2311-00776.creator: H. Gress, J. Barbish, C. Yanik, I. I. Kaya, R. T. Erdogan, M. S. Hanay, M. González, O. Svitelskiy, M. R. Paul, K. L. Ekinci
arxiv-2311-00776.description: Abstract Brownian motion imposes a hard limit on the overall precision of a nanomechanical measurement. Here, we present a combined experimental and theoretical study of the Brownian dynamics of a quintessential nanomechanical system, a doubly-clamped nanomechanical beam resonator, in a viscous fluid.

arxiv-2411-09835.title: Proton removal from 73,75 Br to 72,74 Se at intermediate energies
arxiv-2411-09835.creator: M. Spieker, D. Bazin, S. Biswas, P.D. Cottle, P.J. Farris, A. Gade, T. Ginter, S. Giraud, K.W. Kemper, J. Li, S. Noji, J. Pereira, L.A. Riley, M.K. Smith, D. Weisshaar, R.G.T. Zegers
arxiv-2411-09835.description: Abstract We report new experimental data for excited states of 72,74 Se obtained from proton removal from 73,75 Br secondary beams on a proton target. The experiments were performed with the Ursinus-NSCL Liquid Hydrogen Target and the combined GRETINA+S800 setup at the Coupled Cyclotron Facility of the National Superconducting Cyclotron Laboratory at Michigan State University.

arxiv-2503-19948.title: Test-Time Reasoning Through Visual Human Preferences with VLMs and Soft Rewards
arxiv-2503-19948.creator: Alexander Gambashidze, Konstantin Sobolev, Andrey Kuznetsov, Ivan Oseledets
arxiv-2503-19948.description: Abstract Can Visual Language Models (VLMs) effectively capture human visual preferences? This work addresses this question by training VLMs to think about preferences at test time, employing reinforcement learning methods inspired by DeepSeek R1 and OpenAI O1. Using datasets such as ImageReward and Human Preference Score v2 (HPSv2), our models achieve accuracies of 64.

arxiv-2503-24269.title: A direct detection method of galaxy intrinsic ellipticity-gravitational shear correlation in non-linear regimes using self-calibration
arxiv-2503-24269.creator: Avijit Bera, Leonel Medina Varela, Vinu Sooriyaarachchi, Mustapha Ishak, Carter Williams, and the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration
arxiv-2503-24269.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Avijit Bera, Leonel Medina Varela, Vinu Sooriyaarachchi, Mustapha Ishak, Carter Williams, and the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration. Intrinsic alignment (IA) of galaxies is a challenging source of contamination in the Cosmic shear (GG) signals. The galaxy intrinsic ellipticity-gravitational shear (IG) correlation is generally the most dominant component of such contamination for cross-correlating redshift bins. One of the most effective techniques to mitigate such contamination is the self-calibration (SC) method which extracts the IG correlation and allows for its removal from the GG signal.

arxiv-2504-21650.title: HoloTime: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Panoramic 4D Scene Generation
arxiv-2504-21650.creator: Haiyang Zhou, Wangbo Yu, Jiawen Guan, Xinhua Cheng, Yonghong Tian, Li Yuan
arxiv-2504-21650.description: Abstract . The rapid advancement of diffusion models holds the promise of revolutionizing the application of VR and AR technologies, which typically require scene-level 4D assets for user experience. Nonetheless, existing diffusion models predominantly concentrate on modeling static 3D scenes or object-level dynamics, constraining their capacity to provide truly immersive experiences.

arxiv-2506-13752.title: Steering LLM Thinking with Budget Guidance
arxiv-2506-13752.creator: Junyan Li, Wenshuo Zhao, Yang Zhang, Chuang Gan
arxiv-2506-13752.description: Abstract Recent deep-thinking large language models often reason extensively to improve performance, but such lengthy reasoning is not always desirable, as it incurs excessive inference costs with disproportionate performance gains. Controlling reasoning length without sacrificing performance is therefore important, but remains challenging, especially under tight thinking budgets.

arxiv-2509-23648.title: Emergence of General Relativity from Cosmological Constant Via Ghost Condensation
arxiv-2509-23648.creator: Ichiro Oda Department of Physics, Faculty of Science, University of the Ryukyus, Nishihara, Okinawa 903-0213, Japan
arxiv-2509-23648.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ichiro Oda Department of Physics, Faculty of Science, University of the Ryukyus, Nishihara, Okinawa 903-0213, Japan. We show that starting with a cosmological constant in a curved space-time, the Einstein-Hilbert term of general relativity is generated through a ghost condensation.

arxiv-2510-13186.title: STT-GS: Sample-Then-Transmit Edge Gaussian Splatting with Joint Client Selection and Power Control
arxiv-2510-13186.creator: Zhen Li, Xibin Jin, Guoliang Li, Shuai Wang, Miaowen Wen, Huseyin Arslan, Fellow, IEEE, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Fellow, IEEE, Chengzhong Xu, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2510-13186.description: Abstract Edge Gaussian splatting (EGS), which aggregates data from distributed clients and trains a global GS model at the edge server, is an emerging paradigm for scene reconstruction. Unlike traditional edge resource management methods that emphasize communication throughput or general-purpose learning performance, EGS explicitly aims to maximize the GS qualities, rendering existing approaches inapplicable.

pmc-12605213.title: A novel prognostic tool for triple-negative breast cancer: creating and testing a parthanatos-related gene model
pmc-12605213.creator: Zitong Yang, Siyi Chen, Jiahong Sun, Guangmin Wu, Delu Mu, Jiandong Wang
pmc-12605213.description: BackgroundParthanatos is a poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1)-dependent programmed cell death pathway. However, the association between parthanatos and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as well as its impact on patient prognosis remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the prognostic value of parthanatos in TNBC and to develop a predictive model for identifying potential prognostic biomarkers.

pmc-13169718.title: Evaluation of surgical visualization headset in dental education for preclinical bone augmentation surgery
pmc-13169718.creator: Hao Zeng, Qihang Fan, Ting Xia, Qin Zhao
pmc-13169718.description: BackgroundEffective preclinical training for complex procedures, such as oral bone augmentation, demands high-fidelity visual demonstration. The conventional “display screen combined with a dental microscope” model is limited by inconsistent sightlines, variable viewing angles, and instructor ergonomic challenges. The surgical visualization headset has emerged as a novel technology to provide an immersive, stereoscopic, and synchronized learning view.

pmc-13445834.title: Attitudes of Swedish primary care physicians toward GLP-1 receptor agonists for overweight and obesity: a cross-sectional survey
pmc-13445834.creator: Isabelle Sundell, Björn Wettermark, Anders Sundström, Mats Martinell, Björn Ericsson, Ulf Lindahl, Hussein N Rubaiy, Maria Palmetun Ekbäck
pmc-13445834.description: BackgroundObesity is a growing global health burden, previously with few effective treatments. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) were originally approved for diabetes but are increasingly prescribed for treatment of overweight and obesity.
